subject: GilaTech discovery recap — throughput & SLOs, model footprint, deployment options
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@gilatech.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@gilatech.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / demo follow-up

Thanks for the demo today — quick recap from our side and a few clarifying Qs.

High-level pain points we reiterated:
- High per-call latency on our current in-house endpoint; user-facing agents time out at ~500ms for multi-turn prompts.
- Cost of inference at scale is unpredictable; spikes during batch churn blow our monthly budget.
- Need stronger controls for model version pinning and audit for regulated workflows.

Goals we want to achieve with a partner: 95th percentile latency under 200ms for single-turn prompts (up to 1k tokens), predictable per-token costs with committed capacity, and a private deployment option for our regulated product.

Clarifying questions from engineering:
1) What level of throughput can Redwood Dedicated sustain on an 8x A100 pool with the 7B quantized variant?
2) Do you support prefix/KV caching across sessions for multi-turn agents?
3) How does failover to a smaller quantized variant affect latency SLAs?

I've attached the initial workload profile and a short list of sample prompts (gilatech_poc_requirements.xlsx). Can we schedule a focused ops/infra deep dive next week? Marcus will join from infra.

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Product Engineering
GilaTech

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@gilatech.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@gilatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 17:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro / demo follow-up

Sara — thanks for the crisp summary and the attachment, that helps. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

Short answers:
- Throughput: an 8x A100 Dedicated pool typically sustains ~450–550 req/s for a 7B quantized variant with 512-token context when using our continuous-batching runtime. We can provide a modeled capacity plan once we see the token distribution.
- KV caching: yes — Redwood supports prefix and KV cache across sessions. For multi-turn agents we typically see 30–60% token savings depending on prompt reuse.
- Failover behavior: when routing to a smaller quantized variant we preserve low latency by routing shorter tail requests to the smaller model; however, output quality can change. Our recommended SLOs treat such fallbacks as "graceful degradation" and we track quality regressions per prompt set.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ops deep-dive (60 min) — review workload profile, expected concurrency, and deployment topology (Private vs Dedicated). Recommend scheduling for Tue/Wed next week.
2) Redwood will provide an initial capacity model and a short latency throughput matrix based on the workbook you shared.
3) We'll include Marissa (infrastructure/ops) and Karthik (serving runtime) on the deep dive to address kernel/quantization details and rollout strategy.

I've attached a sketch of the deployment topology we typically propose for regulated workloads (inference_topology_sketch.pdf).

If that matches your plan I'll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read with the questions we need answered to finalize the capacity model.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@gilatech.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@gilatech.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: GilaTech discovery recap — ops deep-dive prep

Forwarding Sara's workbook and a quick internal summary before the call. Please see the pre-read questions I plan to send to GilaTech — want to make sure we cover the runtime knobs and an initial capacity sketch.

=== Internal summary / asks ===
Workload highlights (from workbook):
- Peak concurrent users: ~600 active agents during business hours (US), average session length ~18 turns, median response size ~350 tokens.
- Bursty batch jobs overnight (async classification) with spikes up to 2.5x baseline throughput.

Key engineering asks to cover on call:
- Target SLOs: client asked 95p latency <200ms for single-turn; we should confirm whether 99p is in scope for the MVP. Propose: 95p <200ms, 99p <350ms as a starting point.
- Model variants: start with a high-quality 13B float16 for dev / small percent traffic; primary serving on 7B int8/4-bit quantized variant for cost parity. Need to capture quality delta per prompt set.
- Autoscaling and burst: discuss Dedicated pool sizing + burst to hosted capacity; we should present a hybrid routing option: Dedicated primary, hosted fallback for burst and maintenance windows.
- KV/prefix cache: recommend enabling prefix caching with a 24-hour TTL for agent sessions; quantify expected token savings (we can estimate 30–45% on their sample prompts).
- Compilation/kernel selection: Karthik, please prepare notes on kernel choices for 7B quantized on A100 (cuBLAS/flash attention variants we recommend) + memory footprint per instance.
- Quantization impact: Marissa, can you provide a short note on memory/speed delta between int8 and 4-bit for 7B on an A100? We'll use that for cost modeling.

Attachments to include in pre-read: inference_topology_sketch.pdf (topology options), a 1-pager capacity model template, and the workbook Sara sent.

Can you both confirm availability Tue 11/11 10am PT for a 60-min deep-dive? If not, propose alternatives.

Thanks — I'll send the pre-read to Sara & Marcus after you confirm.

-Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@gilatech.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@gilatech.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Nov 2025 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: GilaTech discovery recap — ops deep-dive prep

Alex / Marissa — 10am PT on Tue 11/11 works for me. I'll bring the following for the call:

- Kernel selection notes: recommended flash-attention kernels for transformer blocks vs cuBLAS matmul fallback; expected latency improvement numbers for 7B quantized on A100 (we've observed ~15–25% lower p95 with flash-attention in our benchmarks).
- Memory footprints: 7B int8 ~7.5 GB resident per replica; 4-bit ~5.2 GB (ballpark).
- Batching guidance: continuous batching config we recommend for sub-200ms p95 with throughput targets up to ~500 req/s; include suggestions for request coalescing and max batching window.
- Fallback routing plan: how quality-first routing vs latency-first routing affects SLOs and a sample A/B rollout plan.

I'll attach a short slide (kernel_and_quant_notes.pdf) to the pre-read and include a quick table mapping capacity (replica counts) to expected p95 latency for their reported median token sizes.

I'll also flag one risk: their overnight batch spikes (2.5x) will need either burst capacity to hosted or pre-provisioned buffer in Dedicated — will quantify cost tradeoffs in the capacity model.

See you Tue — Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
